identity.description: Open, see, click and type in a real browser — read its page, console and network, and drive it in the DevTools protocol.

chip.description: What the browser shows right now, as an image.

contributions.name: browser_open
contributions.description: Open a URL in the browser and return a screenshot. A screenshot's pixels are the coordinates a click takes.

url.description: http(s):// or file:// address to open.

contributions.name: browser_screenshot
contributions.description: Screenshot the browser as it is right now — the viewport, the whole scrollable page, or one element.

fullPage.description: The whole document rather than the viewport.

contributions.name: browser_read_page
contributions.description: What is on the page: an accessibility outline whose interactive parts carry ref_N handles the other tools take, or the page as plain text. Prefer this over measuring a screenshot.

format.description: tree (default): named parts with refs. text: what a person reads.

contributions.name: browser_click
contributions.description: Click an element by its ref, or at screenshot pixels (origin top-left). Returns a fresh screenshot.

x.description: Pixels from the left edge of the screenshot.

y.description: Pixels from the top edge of the screenshot.

count.description: 2 for a double click, 3 for a triple.

modifiers.description: Held while acting: Alt, Ctrl, Meta or Shift.

contributions.name: browser_pointer
contributions.description: Pointer gestures beyond a click: hover to open a menu, scroll a list, or drag one place to another.

x.description: Or screenshot pixels from the left.

y.description: Or screenshot pixels from the top.

toX.description: drag: where to release, in screenshot pixels.

toY.description: drag: where to release, in screenshot pixels.

deltaY.description: scroll: pixels down, negative for up. Default 400.

deltaX.description: scroll: pixels right, negative for left.

contributions.name: browser_key
contributions.description: Press a key — Enter, Tab, Escape, Backspace, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down, space, or a single character — optionally several times and with modifiers held. Returns a fresh screenshot.

modifiers.description: Held while acting: Alt, Ctrl, Meta or Shift.

contributions.name: browser_type
contributions.description: Type a whole string, optionally into a field named by its ref first, and optionally press Enter after. For a select, a checkbox, or replacing an existing value, use browser_fill.

ref.description: Focus this field first, from browser_read_page.

contributions.name: browser_fill
contributions.description: Set a form control to a value — text field, textarea, select (by value or label), or checkbox (true/false). Fires the events a framework listens for, so a React form really does hold the value.

value.description: The value, or true/false for a checkbox.

contributions.name: browser_page
contributions.description: The page itself: go back or forward, reload, wait for something to appear, emulate a device or colour scheme, print to PDF, or hand files to a file input.

selector.description: wait: a CSS selector that must appear.

text.description: wait: text that must appear on the page.

gone.description: wait: a CSS selector that must disappear.

mobile.description: emulate: a phone rather than a desktop.

offline.description: emulate: pretend the network is gone.

ref.description: upload: the file input, from browser_read_page.

files.description: upload: absolute paths to hand it.

contributions.name: browser_console
contributions.description: What the page has logged since it was opened — console calls, uncaught exceptions, and the browser's own complaints (a blocked load, a CSP refusal).

contributions.name: browser_network
contributions.description: What the page asked the network for since it was opened, one line per request. Pass a requestId to read that response's body in full.

urlPattern.description: Keep only requests whose URL contains this.

requestId.description: Read this response body (the #id in a listing).

contributions.name: browser_evaluate
contributions.description: Evaluate a JavaScript expression in the page and return its JSON value — for state a screenshot cannot show, like a score variable.

contributions.name: browser_cdp
contributions.description: Send any Chrome DevTools Protocol command to the page and return its result — Accessibility, DOM, Storage, Performance, Debugger, anything the other tools do not model. With events: true, read the raw event stream instead.

events.description: Read buffered events rather than sending a command.

eventMethod.description: events: a domain (Network) or one method name.

contributions.name: browser_close
contributions.description: Close the browser and end its profile session.

contributions.name: todo_update

contributions.name: todo_read

note.description: What you are about to do.

contributions.name: list_checkpoints

contributions.name: fetch_url

chip.description: What the browser shows right now, as an image.

contributions.name: browser_open
contributions.description: Open a URL in the browser and return a screenshot. A screenshot's pixels are the coordinates a click takes.

url.description: http(s):// or file:// address to open.

contributions.name: browser_screenshot
contributions.description: Screenshot the browser as it is right now — the viewport, the whole scrollable page, or one element.

fullPage.description: The whole document rather than the viewport.

contributions.name: browser_read_page
contributions.description: What is on the page: an accessibility outline whose interactive parts carry ref_N handles the other tools take, or the page as plain text. Prefer this over measuring a screenshot.

format.description: tree (default): named parts with refs. text: what a person reads.

contributions.name: browser_click
contributions.description: Click an element by its ref, or at screenshot pixels (origin top-left). Returns a fresh screenshot.

x.description: Pixels from the left edge of the screenshot.

y.description: Pixels from the top edge of the screenshot.

count.description: 2 for a double click, 3 for a triple.

modifiers.description: Held while acting: Alt, Ctrl, Meta or Shift.

contributions.name: browser_pointer
contributions.description: Pointer gestures beyond a click: hover to open a menu, scroll a list, or drag one place to another.

x.description: Or screenshot pixels from the left.

y.description: Or screenshot pixels from the top.

toX.description: drag: where to release, in screenshot pixels.

toY.description: drag: where to release, in screenshot pixels.

deltaY.description: scroll: pixels down, negative for up. Default 400.

deltaX.description: scroll: pixels right, negative for left.

contributions.name: browser_key
contributions.description: Press a key — Enter, Tab, Escape, Backspace, Delete, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Down, space, or a single character — optionally several times and with modifiers held. Returns a fresh screenshot.

modifiers.description: Held while acting: Alt, Ctrl, Meta or Shift.

contributions.name: browser_type
contributions.description: Type a whole string, optionally into a field named by its ref first, and optionally press Enter after. For a select, a checkbox, or replacing an existing value, use browser_fill.

ref.description: Focus this field first, from browser_read_page.

contributions.name: browser_fill
contributions.description: Set a form control to a value — text field, textarea, select (by value or label), or checkbox (true/false). Fires the events a framework listens for, so a React form really does hold the value.

value.description: The value, or true/false for a checkbox.

contributions.name: browser_page
contributions.description: The page itself: go back or forward, reload, wait for something to appear, emulate a device or colour scheme, print to PDF, or hand files to a file input.

selector.description: wait: a CSS selector that must appear.

text.description: wait: text that must appear on the page.

gone.description: wait: a CSS selector that must disappear.

mobile.description: emulate: a phone rather than a desktop.

offline.description: emulate: pretend the network is gone.

ref.description: upload: the file input, from browser_read_page.

files.description: upload: absolute paths to hand it.

contributions.name: browser_console
contributions.description: What the page has logged since it was opened — console calls, uncaught exceptions, and the browser's own complaints (a blocked load, a CSP refusal).

contributions.name: browser_network
contributions.description: What the page asked the network for since it was opened, one line per request. Pass a requestId to read that response's body in full.

urlPattern.description: Keep only requests whose URL contains this.

requestId.description: Read this response body (the #id in a listing).

contributions.name: browser_evaluate
contributions.description: Evaluate a JavaScript expression in the page and return its JSON value — for state a screenshot cannot show, like a score variable.

contributions.name: browser_cdp
contributions.description: Send any Chrome DevTools Protocol command to the page and return its result — Accessibility, DOM, Storage, Performance, Debugger, anything the other tools do not model. With events: true, read the raw event stream instead.

events.description: Read buffered events rather than sending a command.

eventMethod.description: events: a domain (Network) or one method name.

contributions.name: browser_close
contributions.description: Close the browser and end its profile session.

contributions.name: ios_devices
contributions.description: List the available iOS simulators and their states.

contributions.name: ios_boot
contributions.description: Boot a simulator by udid — the list of devices reports them — and open the Simulator window.

contributions.name: ios_install
contributions.description: Install a built .app bundle onto the booted simulator.

contributions.name: ios_launch
contributions.description: Launch an app by bundle id on the booted simulator, then screenshot it.

contributions.name: ios_screenshot
contributions.description: Screenshot the booted simulator. Tap coordinates use these exact pixels.

contributions.name: ios_tap
contributions.description: Tap the booted simulator at coordinates in the pixels of the screenshots (origin top-left), then return a fresh screenshot.

x.description: Pixels from the left of the screenshot.

y.description: Pixels from the top of the screenshot.

contributions.name: ios_open_url
contributions.description: Open a URL (https:// or a deep link) on the booted simulator.

contributions.name: ios_terminate
contributions.description: Terminate an app by bundle id on the booted simulator.

contributions.name: android_devices
contributions.description: List connected Android devices and running emulators.

contributions.name: android_install
contributions.description: Install an APK onto the connected device or emulator.

contributions.name: android_launch
contributions.description: Launch an app: a package name (com.example.app) or a full component (com.example.app/.MainActivity). Returns a screenshot.

contributions.name: android_screenshot
contributions.description: Screenshot the device. Tap coordinates use these exact pixels.

contributions.name: android_tap
contributions.description: Tap at coordinates in the pixels of the screenshots (origin top-left), then return a fresh screenshot.

contributions.name: android_key
contributions.description: Press a key: ENTER, BACK, HOME, TAB, or any KEYCODE_* name. Returns a screenshot.

contributions.name: android_text
contributions.description: Type text into the focused field, then return a screenshot.

contributions.name: android_logcat
contributions.description: The last lines of logcat, optionally filtered to one tag.

Checkout drops the cart when a 502 hits mid-retry. Find it, fix it, prove it.

summary: Reading the retry path. checkout/retry.ts rebuilds the request on a 5xx, but the body stream was consumed by the first attempt — a retried POST would go out empty. The report fits. Reproducing with the existing test file before changing anything.

item.text: The retry re-sends the request, but the body stream is already spent — a 502 mid-flight retries with an empty cart. Reproducing it first.

approval.reason: Wants to run the test suite in this workspace

options.label: Allow for this session
options.description: Runs without asking again until this session ends.

delta.chunk: ✗ preserves the cart body across retries
→ expected a cart of 3 items, request body was empty

item.output:
❯ src/checkout/retry.test.ts (3 tests | 1 failed) 812ms
   ✓ retries an idempotent GET on 502
   ✓ gives up after three attempts
   ✗ preserves the cart body across retries
     → expected a cart of 3 items, request body was empty

 Tests  1 failed | 2 passed (3)

item.text: Confirmed — it fails exactly where the report says. Buffering the body once, before the first attempt, and re-arming it for every retry.

delta.chunk: ✓ preserves the cart body across retries

item.output:
✓ src/checkout/retry.test.ts (3 tests) 794ms
   ✓ retries an idempotent GET on 502
   ✓ gives up after three attempts
   ✓ preserves the cart body across retries

 Tests  3 passed (3)

item.text: Fixed. The body is buffered once and re-armed for every attempt, so a 502 can no longer empty the cart — retry.ts +9 −2, and the failing test passes.
